annotation.title_clean: “Embodied AI” and the direct participation in hostilities: A legal analysis
annotation.title_en: “Embodied AI” and the direct participation in hostilities: A legal analysis
annotation.venue: Georgetown Journal of International Law, Vol. 51
annotation.summary_en: Law journal article analysing whether civilian embodied AI (robots) can directly participate in hostilities under international humanitarian law. It critiques the ICRC Interpretive Guidance on DPH, proposes a Turing-like test, and explores consequences such as robot PMCs, spies, perfidy, levée en masse and POW status.
key_provisions_or_claims: Questions whether the IHL concept of 'civilian' should be limited to humans.
Challenges the ICRC presumption of civilian status in cases of doubt, favouring case-by-case DPH assessment.
Proposes adding a Turing-like test to DPH assessment.
Applies the ICRC three-part DPH test to scenarios from current to long-term EAI (driverless vehicles, robot medics, personal assistants).
Warns that indistinguishable EAIs on the battlefield may need to be treated as civilians; raises POW and perfidy issues.
